attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No valid extraction theorem converts an arbitrary small circuit for H_N into a small full-witness set, and partial certificates give a concrete counter-mechanism.
steps: Start with the previous necessary condition W_N^*>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} for realized full satisfying witnesses.

Construct the circuit OR_{j,p in P_j} TermSat(F_{N,j}(x),p) after computing all F_{N,j}(x) once; this decides H_N whenever P is a complete satisfying-term cover.
Conclude that full-witness entropy is only a weak necessary condition and must be replaced by tau_N^{term}, or more robustly K_N^{cert}.

branch_outputs.branch_title: High-q generated-OR carrier: partial-certificate cover gate

assumptions: Source lower-bound model is nonuniform Boolean circuit SIZE on N-bit inputs.
Generated queries are CNF encodings so a partial assignment p is a sound certificate when every clause has a literal fixed true by p.
A cover P={P_j} is complete for the generated range when SAT(F_{N,j}(x)) implies some p in P_j satisfies F_{N,j}(x) as a partial assignment.
Verifier overhead for checking a hardwired partial assignment against an L-bit CNF is L^{O(1)}=N^{o(1)}.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M} SAT(F_{N,j}(x)) on N-bit x, with M=N^q, F_{N,j} produced by a shared nonuniform generator G_N of size N^{rho+o(1)}, and each query a CNF of length L=(log N)^d.

target object: CNF-SAT on L-bit formulas, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly only after the generated-OR lower bound and the substitution bridge both remain valid for every fixed target exponent.
controlled interface: if SAT has circuits of size n^c, substitute them into the M generated queries after computing the shared query list once; the source upper bound is N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+o(1)}.

target-preserving condition: require d>1, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, q>(1+epsilon)/2 for dense tuple leakage, uniform query length L=polylog N, and no advice except G_N plus the assumed target SAT circuits.

assumptions: Generated formulas are CNFs over v<=L variables.
Every realized full witness satisfies the generated formula in the ordinary SAT verifier.
Partial assignments are allowed to be hardwired nonuniformly by position j.
Verifier cost is polylogarithmic and hence exponent-negligible.
definitions: W_N^* is the total number of realized full satisfying assignment pairs (j,a) over the generated positive range.
tau_N^{term} is the minimum position-indexed satisfying partial-assignment cover complexity for the same generated range.
A full assignment is a special partial assignment of width v, where v is the variable count of the generated CNF.
The comparison is inside the source model SIZE on H_N, not a claim about SAT lower bounds.

assumptions: Each R_{j,a} has size counted in the source circuit budget.
The generator output can be wired into every selected local predicate.
Soundness prevents false acceptance on negative generated bags.
The audit allows nonuniform hardwiring, matching the SIZE source model.
definitions: K_N^{cert} minimizes the total circuit cost of hardwired predicates R_{j,a}(phi) that are sound for SAT on formulas phi and complete for generated positive queries at position j.
Soundness means R_{j,a}(phi)=1 implies SAT(phi), at least for every formula in the generated range; global soundness is stronger and cleaner.
Completeness means for every x,j with SAT(F_{N,j}(x))=1, some predicate in the position-j list accepts F_{N,j}(x).
This is a source-side nonuniform leakage audit, not a target SAT circuit upper bound.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No target-preserving p-simulation from P or SIZE(poly) into polynomial-size OBDDs exists; the bridge collapses before reaching P vs NP.
steps: Assume a route proves OBDD(SAT_m)>m^a, or even 2^{Omega(m)}, under all variable orders.
Under P=NP we obtain a uniform time m^k SAT decider and hence polynomial-size Boolean circuits for SAT_m.
To contradict the OBDD lower bound, we need a uniform compilation of every such P computation into OBDDs of size below L(m).
HWB_m is in P and has exponential OBDD size for every order, so the needed universal P-to-OBDD compilation is false.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The source lower bound can separate SAT from OBDD(poly), but it does not exclude polynomial-time algorithms or polynomial circuits for SAT.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: OBDD Target Gate

assumptions: OBDD size is deterministic and exact; randomized or nondeterministic branching programs require a separate model audit.
If a fixed variable order is used, the target class must include that same fixed-order restriction; otherwise quantify over all orders.
Karp reductions are not automatically OBDD-friendly; projections or read-once substitutions need separate preservation proofs.
The route is outside no known barrier merely by being combinatorial; the obstruction here is target-model simulation, not relativization folklore.
definitions: source object: a deterministic OBDD lower bound L(m) for SAT_m or another NP-complete Boolean function on m input bits, preferably minimizing over all variable orders.
target object: P versus NP, formalized as excluding every uniform polynomial-time decider for SAT, not merely excluding OBDD or read-once branching programs.
controlled interface: a compiler mapping each target computation of time or circuit size s(m) to an equivalent OBDD of size B_C(m,s), with variable-order advice explicitly counted.
target-preserving condition: for every polynomial target bound s=m^k, the source lower bound must satisfy L(m)>B_C(m,s) after reductions, padding, and order conventions are preserved.

equations.label: restricted_transfer
equations.valid_when: Valid when every size-s target computation in C has a proved OBDD compilation of size at most B_C(m,s).

equations.label: pnp_assumption_only_gives_circuits
equations.valid_when: Applies only after assuming a uniform polynomial-time SAT decider and using the standard time-to-circuit simulation.

equations.label: compiler_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Valid for deterministic OBDDs minimizing over variable orders and the standard hidden-weighted-bit function.

candidate_lemmas.statement: An OBDD lower bound is a valid bridge only to target classes with a proved OBDD compilation bound. A superpolynomial OBDD lower bound for SAT does not imply P != NP; the missing P-to-OBDD compiler is falsified by HWB in P.

control_decision.pivot_test: If a future branching-program route cannot prove an OBDD compilation bound for its target class, quarantine it as a restricted-model separation.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the route states C, proves B_C(m,s), and shows L(m)>B_C after reductions and advice accounting.

dependency_updates.description: OBDD lower bounds require a compiler from the target class to OBDDs; no such compiler exists for P or SIZE(poly).
Variable-order advice must be quantified over or counted; fixed-order lower bounds do not target best-order OBDDs.
The failure is not an oracle-barrier contradiction but a false target-model containment.

falsifiers: HWB_m is the decisive falsifier: it lies in P yet has OBDD size 2^{Omega(m)} for every variable order.
Polynomial-size circuits can compute functions with exponential OBDD size, so SIZE(poly) is not contained in OBDD(poly).
Standard many-one reductions can destroy OBDD structure; NP-completeness alone is not an OBDD-preserving transfer certificate.
Per-length variable-order advice can leak nonuniform power; fixed-order lower bounds are invalid for best-order OBDD targets unless advice is controlled.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The route still lacks a source theorem proving either an actual MCSP-hard canonical row or an unrestricted aggregate lower bound above q_force with cap slack.
steps: Assume every row is easy: C(T_{m,r})<=2^{epsilon m}. Hardwire the M_m row circuits and select by r; this gives C(A_m)<=2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)}.
Therefore an unrestricted aggregate lower bound C(A_m)>2^{q(d_m+m)} forces a hard row only when q(1+D)>D+epsilon.
If such a hard row exists directly, the multiplexed target already has lower bound exponent epsilon/(1+D) on core lengths, and kappa-padding gives delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).

Trying to replace the unrestricted aggregate lower bound by uniform decoder hardness fails: nonuniform circuits can hardwire row circuits, and constant-row or easy-row aggregates defeat the implication.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: These are conditional bridge and quarantine lemmas. They identify valid transfer thresholds and falsifiers but do not construct the required non-natural, advice-free MCSP source, so they do not prove P != NP.

assumptions: Source lengths form a kappa-dense infinite set, or an all-length padded schedule with the same multiplicative loss.
Distinct-image unranking runs in 2^{O(m)} time, so the multiplexed target language is in E.
For every usable m, at least one canonical row has MCSP no-side threshold C(T)>2^{epsilon m}.
No nonuniform selector or advice is used to choose m, r, or a duplicate representative.
definitions: source object: For source length m, V_m is an E-uniform certificate verifier/emitter whose distinct accepted images are truth tables T_{m,r}:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, r<M_m, with M_m<=2^{D m+o(m)}.
target object: L_V is the padded multiplexed E language whose core maps (r,x) to T_{m,r}(x), with |r|=ceil(log M_m) and |x|=m.

controlled interface: Parameters epsilon,D,kappa and an E-canonical distinct-image unranking algorithm; on each source length there is an accepted row T_{m,r} with unrestricted circuit complexity C(T_{m,r})>2^{epsilon m}.

target-preserving condition: The source length schedule, row ranks, unranking, and padding are uniform and advice-free; padding changes only input length and preserves the nonuniform circuit lower-bound implication.
kappa-density means successive usable core lengths grow by at most a factor kappa+o(1).
The row complexity C(T) is unrestricted Boolean circuit size for the m-input function whose truth table is T.
